title: AKS Automatic, and what Microsoft takes over

videos.script: Lesson 11 left you a cluster full of decisions. The tier, the pools, the size of every machine, the upgrade channels. This lesson is about AKS Automatic, which makes them for you. {{sku}} It is the same AKS, and the same Kubernetes. One property changes, the SKU, and with it a long list of settings becomes preconfigured. That word means on, and not yours to change. {{nap}} The first is the nodes. There are no pools to size. Node auto-provisioning watches for pods that cannot be scheduled, picks a machine that would hold them, and creates it. It is Karpenter, run by AKS. {{safeguards}} The second is what you may deploy. Deployment safeguards check every manifest as it arrives. No requests, no probes, or an image tagged latest, and the cluster refuses it, or rewrites it. {{giveup}} Then the price of all that. No way into the nodes, no Free tier, no stopping the cluster at night, and a bill that follows the requests in your manifests. {{kind}} kind has no Karpenter and no Azure Policy. So the lab shows the Kubernetes they react to: a pod left pending, a NodePool checked by the API server, and the shop's manifest before and after.
